description: [The Conversation Africa] When COVID hit, healthcare systems around the world were turned upside down. Hospitals cleared beds, routine appointments were cancelled and people were told to stay at home unless it was urgent. In England, visits to family doctors and hospital admissions for non-COVID reasons fell by a third in the early months of the pandemic. Medical staff were redeployed, routine clinics were cancelled and diagnostic tests were postponed.
title: Africa: The Pandemic's Hidden Toll - Millions of Chronic Conditions Left Undiagnosed

title: Africa: The Year Ahead for African Democracy - Who Is Going to the Polls in 2026?

title: Africa: The Somaliland Paradox - Why the World Can No Longer Afford to Ignore Africa's Most Successful State
